name: ML Systems Taxonomy
citation: Vijay Janapa Reddi. ML Systems Taxonomy, version 0.3-draft. Machine Learning Systems, 2026. https://mlsysbook.ai/taxonomy/
note: Editorial draft for expert review; not a claim of completeness or consensus.
tagging_rules: Tag an item with the concepts it centrally teaches or tests: prefer one, and add a second or third only when the item cannot be answered without it. Do not tag prerequisites or passing mentions.
Tag a subject alone when the item covers the subject broadly or no concept is specific enough. A subject tag is a valid, complete tag.
When no concept fits, tag the closest subject and record the missing idea as a proposed concept; proposals feed the next version.
Store concept identities (mlsys.kv-cache) and subject identities, not codes; codes can be renumbered between versions and identities cannot.
When a concept seems to belong to two subjects, use its home and follow the home rule and its worked examples; related subjects are navigation, not alternative tags.
Do not tag a workload-class concept (Large language model, Transformer) only because the item involves one; tag it when the item is about that workload class.

Tag the mechanism, not the platform. Cloud, edge, mobile, and TinyML are contexts. Use Edge & embedded hardware or On-device deployment as the subject only when the item is about the device class itself or about converting, packaging, or updating models for it, not when a device is merely where a memory, interconnect, or scheduling question arises.

Tag a calculation by what it is about. An estimate of KV-cache size is about the KV cache. Use Performance models, Workload characterization, or Profiling as the subject only when the item teaches the modeling or measurement method itself.
When an item asks for the effect of a technique (the energy saved by INT8, the throughput gained by batching), the technique is the subject and the affected quantity may be a second concept.
Depth is recorded separately (for example, StaffML levels L1 to L6+). A competency is a concept or subject paired with a depth.

When a concept is retired, its identity maps to the concept named in replaced_by. When a concept is split, the old identity is retired and existing tags are re-reviewed; until then they resolve to the replacement.

groups.label: Foundations
groups.question: What does the system compute, what must it achieve, and how do we reason about its cost?

areas.label: Workloads & requirements
areas.question: What must the system achieve, for which workload, and how is success decided?
areas.scope: Targets, workload descriptions, and objectives that every later engineering choice is judged against.

subjects.label: Requirements, SLOs & baselines
subjects.definition: Stating measurable targets for a system's behavior and service, and the baselines and budgets against which they are judged.
includes: Acceptance criteria and baselines
SLIs, SLOs, error budgets
Latency budgets across a request path

subjects.label: Workload characterization
subjects.definition: Describing a workload's compute, memory, data, and traffic demands, and where it runs, so it can be engineered and provisioned for.
includes: FLOP, byte, and memory accounting
Deployment tiers from cloud to TinyML
Workload traces

subjects.label: Objectives, proxies & decision policies
subjects.definition: How learned outputs become decisions, how optimized proxies relate to intended outcomes, and how competing objectives are traded.
includes: Proxy objectives and reward hacking
Cost-sensitive thresholds
Multi-objective tradeoffs

areas.label: Models & architectures
areas.question: What does the model compute, and how does its structure set system cost?
areas.scope: Model families, building blocks, and architectural choices viewed as workloads, plus the artifacts that carry them.

subjects.label: Model families
subjects.definition: The classical and neural model regimes, with their inductive assumptions, viewed as workloads with characteristic compute and memory profiles.
includes: Classical models and neural networks
Transformers, recommendation models, diffusion models

subjects.label: Architecture building blocks
subjects.definition: The layer-level operations from which neural models are composed and whose shapes determine compute, memory, and data movement.
includes: Embeddings, attention, position encoding, tokenization
Convolution, recurrence, normalization

subjects.label: Sparse & conditional computation
subjects.definition: Model designs in which the computation performed varies per input, such as mixture-of-experts routing and early exit.
includes: Mixture of experts, routing, capacity, load balancing
Active vs. total parameters
Early exit

subjects.label: Long-context & efficient sequence models
subjects.definition: Sequence architectures that change how cost scales with context length, co-designed with the memory and compute they demand.
includes: Sparse, sliding-window, and linear attention
State-space models; grouped-query attention
Context-length extension
excludes: Exact attention kernels such as FlashAttention ([[tensor-operators]])

subjects.label: Model artifacts & formats
subjects.definition: The weights, graphs, metadata, and interface contracts that make a trained model a portable, loadable, deployable artifact.
includes: Weight serialization and exchange formats
Model export and signatures

areas.label: Quantitative system models
areas.question: Which simple models predict where time, memory, and money go?
areas.scope: Analytical and empirical models used to bound performance, capacity, and training cost before or instead of measuring.

subjects.label: Roofline, performance models & simulation
subjects.definition: Bound-based reasoning about whether computation is limited by arithmetic or data movement, and how reuse changes that limit.
includes: Ridge point and compute- vs. memory-bound regimes
Energy cost of data movement

subjects.label: Amdahl's law & scaling efficiency
subjects.definition: Models of how much speedup added parallel or accelerated resources can deliver, given serial work and fixed or growing problem sizes.
includes: Amdahl's law and serial fractions
Strong and weak scaling
Parallel efficiency

subjects.label: Queueing & capacity models
subjects.definition: Models relating arrivals, service rates, utilization, and waiting, used to predict latency and capacity under load.
includes: Little's law
Latency-throughput curves
Burstiness and variability
excludes: Measuring a specific serving system's latency and throughput ([[latency-goodput]])

subjects.label: Scaling laws & compute-optimal allocation
subjects.definition: Empirical relationships among parameters, data, and compute and observed quality, used to allocate training budgets.
includes: Loss scaling laws
Compute-optimal model/data allocation
Training compute estimates

groups.label: Stack
groups.question: What does the system run on, from silicon to the fleet?

areas.label: Hardware & accelerators
areas.question: How do processors, memory, and chip-level power shape what ML workloads can achieve?
areas.scope: Compute, memory, interconnect, and power characteristics of ML hardware from datacenter accelerators to microcontrollers.

subjects.label: Accelerator architecture
subjects.definition: The organization of processors specialized for ML: execution units, threading, dataflow, and the throughput they provide.
includes: GPUs, TPUs, NPUs; SIMT and matrix engines
Systolic arrays and dataflows
Domain-specific architectures

subjects.label: Memory hierarchy & bandwidth
subjects.definition: The storage levels of an ML processor, from registers and SRAM to HBM, and the capacity and bandwidth limits they impose.
includes: On-chip SRAM and scratchpads
HBM
The memory wall

subjects.label: Host-device & scale-up interconnect
subjects.definition: Links that move data between hosts and accelerators and among accelerators within a node or rack-scale domain.
includes: PCIe host links
NVLink-class scale-up fabrics
CXL and peer-to-peer transfers

subjects.label: Chip power & thermal limits
subjects.definition: Electrical and thermal limits at the chip and board level, and the runtime controls that keep execution within them.
includes: TDP and thermal throttling
DVFS and power capping
Dark silicon

subjects.label: Edge & embedded hardware
subjects.definition: Hardware for on-device ML, from mobile SoCs to microcontrollers, where memory and energy per inference bind.
includes: Microcontrollers and TinyML devices
Heterogeneous mobile SoCs and NPUs
Energy and memory budgets

areas.label: Frameworks, compilers & runtimes
areas.question: How is a model program expressed, transformed, and executed efficiently on hardware?
areas.scope: The software layers between model code and hardware: programming models, operators, compilers, runtimes, and numerics.

subjects.label: ML frameworks & programming models
subjects.definition: The abstractions with which ML programs are written: tensors, computation graphs, execution modes, and automatic differentiation.
includes: Tensors and computation graphs
Eager vs. graph execution; tracing JIT
Automatic differentiation

subjects.label: Tensor operators & memory layout
subjects.definition: Implementations of core tensor operations, such as matrix multiply, convolution, and attention, and the layouts that govern their efficiency.
includes: GEMM and convolution lowering
IO-aware attention kernels
Vendor kernel libraries

subjects.label: Kernel & GPU programming model
subjects.definition: How kernels are written for parallel accelerators: the thread hierarchy, memory access patterns, occupancy, asynchronous data movement, and programming the matrix units.
includes: Writing and tuning kernels in CUDA-class or tile-level languages such as Triton
Shared memory, synchronization, and latency hiding

subjects.label: ML compilers & kernel optimization
subjects.definition: Transforming model programs through intermediate representations into optimized kernels for target hardware.
includes: Graph and loop IRs; lowering
Fusion, tiling, autotuning, kernel DSLs
Static memory planning

subjects.label: Runtime execution & dispatch
subjects.definition: How a runtime launches and orders device work and manages device memory during execution.
includes: Launch overhead and graph replay
Streams and asynchronous execution
Caching allocators

subjects.label: Data loading & input pipelines
subjects.definition: Delivering training and inference inputs to accelerators fast enough: host-side loading and preprocessing, prefetching, and sampling minibatches from large or irregular data such as graphs.
includes: Data-loader workers, decoding and augmentation on the host, pinned memory, and prefetching
Minibatch construction for irregular data, such as graph neighborhood sampling
excludes: Storage systems and parallel file systems that hold the data ([[storage-systems]])

subjects.label: Numerical formats & precision
subjects.definition: Number formats used in ML computation and the techniques that keep training and inference accurate at reduced precision.
includes: FP32/BF16/FP8/INT formats and block scaling
Mixed precision and loss scaling
Accumulation precision

areas.label: Parallelism & distributed execution
areas.question: How is one workload split across many devices, and what does coordination cost?
areas.scope: Partitioning ML work across devices and participants, the communication it requires, and the coordination that keeps it consistent.

subjects.label: Parallelism strategies
subjects.definition: Ways of partitioning a model's computation and state across devices, and how those dimensions are combined.
includes: Data, tensor, pipeline, sequence, expert parallelism
ZeRO/FSDP state sharding
Hybrid 3D layouts and pipeline bubbles
excludes: Searching for and placing a parallel plan ([[parallelism-planning]])

subjects.label: Parallelization planning & placement
subjects.definition: Choosing and changing how a model is partitioned across devices: describing devices as a mesh, searching or propagating sharding decisions, placing experts and stages on heterogeneous hardware, and resharding at run time.
includes: Automatic parallelization and sharding propagation
Device meshes, expert placement, and dynamic resharding

subjects.label: Collective communication
subjects.definition: Group communication primitives and algorithms used by parallel ML, their cost models, and techniques to reduce or hide their cost.
includes: All-reduce, all-gather, all-to-all
Ring and tree algorithms; alpha-beta cost model
Overlap and gradient compression

subjects.label: Coordination & consensus
subjects.definition: Mechanisms by which distributed components agree on authoritative control state and tolerate stale or failed participants.
includes: Consensus and leader election
Leases and fencing
Bounded-staleness consistency

subjects.label: Federated & decentralized learning
subjects.definition: Training across devices or organizations that keep their data local, coordinated through a shared model.
includes: Federated averaging
Client heterogeneity and selection
Cross-device vs. cross-silo

areas.label: Datacenter infrastructure & fleet
areas.question: How are AI datacenters built, connected, fed, and shared across many jobs?
areas.scope: Facilities, networks, storage, and cluster management that turn many accelerators into a shared ML fleet.

subjects.label: Datacenter power, cooling & facilities
subjects.definition: Engineering of the buildings that house ML fleets: power provisioning, cooling, density, and facility efficiency.
includes: Facility power and oversubscription
Air and liquid cooling; rack density
PUE

subjects.label: Network fabrics
subjects.definition: Datacenter networks that connect accelerator nodes: transports, topologies, flow and congestion control, and in-network compute.
includes: RDMA over InfiniBand and RoCE; lossless flow control
Fat-tree, rail-optimized, torus topologies
Congestion control; in-network reduction

subjects.label: Storage & data delivery
subjects.definition: Storage systems that hold training data, checkpoints, and artifacts at scale and deliver them to accelerators fast enough.
includes: Parallel file systems and object stores
Input pipelines and data stalls
Checkpoint I/O and storage tiering
excludes: Host-side loading and prefetching of batches ([[data-loading]])

subjects.label: Cluster scheduling & orchestration
subjects.definition: Allocating a shared cluster's accelerators to jobs over time: placement, gang allocation, fairness, preemption, and elasticity.
includes: Gang scheduling and backfill
Fair sharing, preemption, elastic jobs
Topology-aware placement and bin packing
excludes: Packaging code and dependencies as images ([[pipelines-reproducibility]])

subjects.label: Capacity planning & multi-tenancy
subjects.definition: Provisioning fleet capacity and sharing it among tenants through quotas, accelerator sharing, and interference control.
includes: Capacity planning and quotas
Accelerator sharing and partitioning
Spot capacity and interference

groups.label: Lifecycle
groups.question: What do engineers do to build, ship, and keep the system working?

areas.label: Data engineering
areas.question: How is data acquired, labeled, curated, validated, stored, and kept trustworthy?
areas.scope: Acquisition and labeling, corpus curation, validation and features, pipelines and storage formats, lineage, and temporal correctness of training and serving data.

subjects.label: Data collection & labeling
subjects.definition: Obtaining observations and supervisory targets whose sampling, coverage, and label quality are known and fit the task.
includes: Sampling design, human and programmatic labeling, labeling budgets.
Annotation quality and agreement.

subjects.label: Data selection & curation
subjects.definition: Choosing, filtering, deduplicating, mixing, augmenting, and synthesizing training examples to maximize learning value per unit of compute and labeling cost.
includes: Web-scale corpus filtering, deduplication, and domain mixtures.
Augmentation and synthetic or model-generated data.
Trajectory and demonstration curation for agents and robots.

subjects.label: Data validation & feature engineering
subjects.definition: Checking that recorded data is fit for use and transforming it into model inputs whose semantics and availability match training and serving.
includes: Schema and distribution checks before training and serving.
Feature construction and shared feature stores.

subjects.label: Data pipelines & storage formats
subjects.definition: Engineering ingestion, batch and stream transformation, event-time semantics, storage formats, and schemas for training and serving data.
includes: ETL/ELT, batch and stream processing, columnar formats.
Data loaders that keep accelerators fed.

subjects.label: Data contracts, versioning & lineage
subjects.definition: Specifying, versioning, and tracing the datasets a system consumes so that dependencies, provenance, and changes are explicit.
includes: Dataset versions, snapshots, and provenance records.
Producer-consumer contracts and dependency hygiene.

subjects.label: Leakage & training-serving skew
subjects.definition: Ensuring examples use only information available at prediction time and that training and serving compute features identically and equally fresh.
includes: Point-in-time joins and temporal leakage.
Feature staleness and skew between offline and online paths.

areas.label: Training & adaptation
areas.question: How are models trained and adapted, and what does that demand from the system?
areas.scope: Learning paradigms, optimization dynamics, training memory, experiment management, fine-tuning, post-training, and continual learning.

subjects.label: Learning paradigms
subjects.definition: The ways supervision, self-generated targets, interaction, and demonstration produce learning signals, each with distinct data and compute demands.
includes: Supervised, self-supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and imitation learning.
excludes: Preference and RL post-training of pretrained models ([[post-training]])

subjects.label: Optimization & training dynamics
subjects.definition: The objectives, update rules, schedules, and batch regimes that determine whether and how efficiently training converges.
includes: Optimizers, learning-rate warmup and decay, large-batch scaling.
Loss spikes, divergence, and their mitigations.

subjects.label: Training memory & state
subjects.definition: Accounting for and reducing the parameters, gradients, optimizer state, and activations a training step must hold.
includes: Activation recomputation, gradient accumulation, CPU/NVMe offload.

subjects.label: Hyperparameter search & experiment management
subjects.definition: Allocating a finite budget of training runs across configurations, and recording runs so their outcomes can be compared and reproduced.
includes: Random, Bayesian, and multi-fidelity search; small-scale proxies.
Run metadata and experiment tracking.

subjects.label: Adaptation: fine-tuning, prompting & transfer
subjects.definition: Adapting a pretrained model to a new task or behavior, by continued training of all or part of its parameters or by prompting without parameter updates.
includes: Instruction and supervised fine-tuning, adapters and LoRA.

subjects.label: Preference & RL post-training
subjects.definition: Training pretrained models against preference, reward-model, or verifiable-reward signals, and the rollout, scoring, and weight-synchronization systems that loop requires.
includes: RLHF, DPO-style preference optimization, RL with verifiable rewards.
Rollout generation, reward scoring, colocated vs disaggregated actor/learner, weight sync.
excludes: Reward exploitation as a specification failure ([[objectives-decisions]])

subjects.label: Continual & online learning
subjects.definition: Updating deployed models incrementally from new or streaming data while retaining prior competence.
includes: Online and incremental updates, forgetting and replay.
Personalization and adaptation on device.

areas.label: Model evaluation & testing
areas.question: How do we know a model and the system around it behave well enough, and for whom?
areas.scope: Evaluation design, metrics and uncertainty, slices and robustness, evaluation of generative and agentic outputs, and ML testing and debugging.

subjects.label: Evaluation design & experiments
subjects.definition: Constructing offline splits and online experiments whose comparisons support the conclusions drawn from them.
includes: Holdout, temporal, and cross-validation splits.
A/B tests, sequential monitoring, interference between units.

subjects.label: Metrics, calibration & uncertainty
subjects.definition: Specifying what is measured and quantifying how far estimates and predicted probabilities can be trusted.
includes: Task metrics, calibration, confidence intervals, abstention.
Distribution-free prediction sets.

subjects.label: Sliced & robustness evaluation
subjects.definition: Measuring behavior separately across populations and conditions, and under deliberate shift or perturbation, rather than only in aggregate.
includes: Subgroup and condition slices, shift and perturbation tests.

subjects.label: Evaluating generative & agentic systems
subjects.definition: Assessing open-ended outputs and multi-step runs where no single reference answer exists, using graders, sampling-aware metrics, and contamination controls.
includes: Model graders, pairwise and human preference, pass@k.
Contamination of benchmarks by training data.
excludes: Verifiers used to select outputs at inference ([[test-time-compute]])

subjects.label: ML testing & debugging
subjects.definition: Testing data, models, pipelines, and their integration against stated expectations when exact expected outputs are often unknown.
includes: Oracles, metamorphic and behavioral tests, readiness rubrics.

areas.label: Deployment & serving
areas.question: How are trained models delivered to users within latency, throughput, and cost targets?
areas.scope: Serving architectures, latency and goodput, request scheduling, LLM inference mechanisms, structured generation, test-time compute, retrieval, and on-device deployment.

subjects.label: Serving architectures
subjects.definition: The structure through which predictions are produced and delivered, from offline batch scoring to online and serverless model servers, multi-model and multi-adapter hosting, and streaming speech services.
includes: Batch vs online prediction, inference servers and APIs.
excludes: Routing and composing calls across models ([[compound-ai]])

subjects.label: Compound AI systems & model routing
subjects.definition: Composing several models, retrievers, and tools into one application, and routing, cascading, caching, and gating requests across models to meet quality and cost targets.
includes: Language-model programs and their optimization
Model routing, cascades, gateways, and semantic caches
excludes: Agent loops that plan and act through tools ([[agent-harness]])

subjects.label: Latency, throughput & goodput
subjects.definition: Defining and meeting per-request latency and useful-throughput targets, including tail behavior and token-level latency for generative services.
includes: Latency budgets, tail latency, TTFT and inter-token latency.
Tail-tolerant request techniques.
excludes: General measurement methodology and profiling ([[profiling-utilization]]); analytic queueing models ([[queueing-models]])

subjects.label: Batching, admission & autoscaling
subjects.definition: Policies that group, admit, distribute, and provision for requests so a service meets its targets under varying load.
includes: Dynamic and iteration-level batching, admission, load balancing.
Autoscaling and model cold start.

subjects.label: LLM & generative inference
subjects.definition: Mechanisms specific to generative inference: managing attention state, separating prompt processing from token generation, accelerating autoregressive decoding, and reducing iterative denoising cost.
includes: KV cache management, prefix reuse, speculative decoding.
Chunked prefill and prefill/decode disaggregation.
Denoising-step reduction and feature caching for diffusion models.

subjects.label: Decoding, sampling & structured output
subjects.definition: Controlling how tokens are selected and constraining generated output to required syntax or schemas.
includes: Temperature and nucleus sampling, grammar-constrained decoding, schema checks.

subjects.label: Test-time compute
subjects.definition: Spending additional inference computation on reasoning, sampling, search, and verification to raise output quality under a budget.
includes: Reasoning budgets, parallel sampling and selection, verifiers, tree search.
Trading inference compute against model size.
excludes: Agent control loops and tool use ([[agent-harness]])

subjects.label: Retrieval & vector search
subjects.definition: Selecting relevant records from an external corpus by lexical, dense, or hybrid search and supplying them to a model at inference.
includes: Retrieval-augmented generation, ANN indexes and vector stores, reranking.
excludes: Agent memory write and consolidation policy ([[context-memory]])

subjects.label: On-device & edge deployment
subjects.definition: Converting, packaging, executing, and updating models on phones, embedded devices, and microcontrollers under memory, energy, and connectivity limits.
includes: Export and conversion, on-device runtimes, device/cloud split.
Over-the-air model updates across heterogeneous fleets.

areas.label: MLOps & operations
areas.question: How is a deployed ML system versioned, observed, changed, and eventually retired?
areas.scope: Release management, monitoring, drift and retraining, incident response, pipelines and reproducibility, platforms and teams, and retirement.

subjects.label: Versioning, rollout & rollback
subjects.definition: Identifying, gating, and progressively exposing model releases, with the ability to return to a known-good configuration.
includes: Registries, CI/CD for models, release gates.
Shadow, canary, and staged rollout; rollback.

subjects.label: Monitoring & observability
subjects.definition: Instrumenting deployed systems and detecting, from logged signals, changes in inputs, outputs, quality, and health.
includes: Prediction logging, drift statistics, alerting and alert fatigue.
Metrics, logs, traces for model services and agents.

subjects.label: Drift, feedback loops & retraining
subjects.definition: Understanding how deployment data and outcomes change, including changes the system itself causes, and deciding when and how to update the model.
includes: Covariate and concept drift, delayed labels, hidden feedback loops.
Scheduled and triggered retraining, continuous training.

subjects.label: Incident response
subjects.definition: Detecting, triaging, mitigating, and learning from production failures, including attributing them to data, model, or infrastructure causes.
includes: Triage, mitigation, blameless postmortems, on-call.

subjects.label: ML pipelines & reproducibility
subjects.definition: Automating the steps that produce models and controlling their environments and configuration so runs can be repeated.
includes: Orchestrated pipelines, environment pinning, configuration as code.

subjects.label: ML platforms, teams & technical debt
subjects.definition: Shared internal platforms, team structures, and debt management that let an organization operate many models at sustainable cost.
includes: Platform-as-product, maturity levels, ownership and roles.
ML-specific technical debt and anti-patterns.

subjects.label: Model retirement
subjects.definition: Ending a model's service by migrating its consumers, archiving what must be kept, and deleting data and resources that are no longer justified.
includes: Deprecation with consumer migration, archival for audit, retention and deletion.
excludes: Removing learned influence of specific records ([[privacy-dp]])

groups.label: Qualities
groups.question: By which properties is the system judged, and how are they engineered?

areas.label: Performance, efficiency & benchmarking
areas.question: How do we measure, compare, and reduce the time, memory, and energy a workload consumes?
areas.scope: Measuring and benchmarking where time, memory, and energy go, and the cross-layer techniques whose primary purpose is to reduce them, such as compression and hardware-aware design.

subjects.label: Profiling & utilization
subjects.definition: Measuring where execution time and resources go under a stated workload, and expressing how much of the hardware's capacity does useful model work.
includes: Profilers and execution-time breakdowns
Utilization metrics such as MFU and training goodput
Bottleneck attribution across compute, memory, I/O, and communication
excludes: Standardized benchmark suites and reporting rules ([[system-benchmarking]])

subjects.label: System benchmarking
subjects.definition: Measuring training and inference system performance under specified workloads, quality targets, load scenarios, and run rules so results are comparable.
includes: MLPerf-style time-to-quality and scenario-based inference metrics.

subjects.label: Model compression
subjects.definition: Techniques that shrink a trained or training model's parameters, precision, or rank to reduce memory, compute, and latency at a measured cost in quality.
includes: Quantization (post-training and quantization-aware)
Pruning (structured and unstructured) and sparsity exploitation
Knowledge distillation and low-rank factorization
excludes: Numeric format definitions and mixed-precision training ([[numerics]])
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning such as LoRA, whose purpose is adaptation ([[fine-tuning]])

subjects.label: Hardware-aware model design
subjects.definition: Choosing or searching model architectures against a target device's measured cost, so that quality and efficiency are optimized together rather than compressed after the fact.
includes: Neural architecture search, including hardware-aware objectives
Efficient building blocks and the accuracy-efficiency frontier
Joint model and hardware co-design

areas.label: Reliability & fault tolerance
areas.question: How does the system keep working, or fail safely, when components fail at scale?
areas.scope: Infrastructure and service fault tolerance, from failure assumptions and recovery semantics to fleet failure rates, checkpoint economics, and resilience testing.

subjects.label: Failure models, retries & degradation
subjects.definition: Declared failure assumptions and the service-level mechanisms (retries, idempotency, replication, circuit breaking, degradation) that keep requests correct and available when components fail.
includes: Failure models and recovery semantics (idempotency, compensation)
Retries, circuit breakers, replication, and failover
Graceful degradation of quality or features under failure
excludes: Physical safety fallbacks and stopping envelopes ([[runtime-enforcement]])

subjects.label: Checkpointing & elastic recovery
subjects.definition: Persisting recoverable state for long-running jobs and choosing checkpoint frequency and recovery strategy to minimize lost work and restart cost under a given failure rate.
includes: Checkpoints and consistent cuts for distributed state
Optimal checkpoint interval (Young-Daly) and asynchronous checkpointing
Elastic recovery on a changed set of workers
excludes: Activation recomputation, sometimes called gradient checkpointing ([[training-memory]])
Checkpoint storage bandwidth and I/O systems ([[storage-systems]])

subjects.label: Hardware faults & silent data corruption
subjects.definition: How hardware fails in a fleet, from fail-stop crashes to gray and silent faults, how often it fails, and how such faults are detected and contained.
includes: Fail-stop, gray, and silent failures and their detection
Fleet failure rates (MTBF composition) and availability
Correlated failures and failure domains
excludes: Chip power and thermal limits as design constraints ([[chip-power-thermal]])

subjects.label: Fault injection & resilience testing
subjects.definition: Deliberately introducing software, infrastructure, or hardware faults under controlled scope to verify that detection, recovery, and degradation work as designed.
includes: Chaos engineering and failure injection in production-like settings
Game days and recovery rehearsals
Hardware fault injection to estimate model error resilience
excludes: Functional ML tests and test oracles ([[ml-testing]])

areas.label: Security & privacy
areas.question: How do we protect ML systems and the data they touch from adversaries and leakage?
areas.scope: Adversaries and defenses across data, model, artifact, and execution boundaries, and the leakage of information about people or records through learned systems.

subjects.label: Threat models & adversarial attacks
subjects.definition: Specifying adversaries against learned systems and the attacks they mount on training data, model inputs, and instruction boundaries, with the defenses aimed at each.
includes: Threat models for ML assets and interfaces
Poisoning, backdoors, evasion, jailbreaks, and prompt injection
Defenses such as adversarial training
excludes: Theft and integrity of model artifacts ([[model-supply-chain]])

subjects.label: Model & supply-chain security
subjects.definition: Protecting models as valuable artifacts from theft and tampering, and protecting the chain of datasets, pretrained weights, libraries, and builds that produce them.
includes: Model extraction and ownership evidence (watermarking)
Artifact signing and provenance
Malicious weights, serialization formats, and dependencies
excludes: Artifact versioning and registries as release tooling ([[release-management]])
Data lineage as a data-engineering practice ([[data-lineage]])

subjects.label: Privacy leakage & differential privacy
subjects.definition: Privacy requirements for data about people, the attacks that extract it from models and outputs, and formal or architectural mechanisms that bound or remove that leakage.
includes: Membership inference and model inversion
Differential privacy and DP-SGD
Machine unlearning and secure aggregation
excludes: Federated training protocols and client scheduling ([[federated-learning]])

subjects.label: Access control & isolation
subjects.definition: Constraining who may act, what code may reach, and which parties can observe data in use, through authorization, least privilege, isolation, and hardware-rooted trust.
includes: Authorization, least privilege, and sandboxed execution
Confidential computing and remote attestation
Side channels across shared accelerators and caches
excludes: Tenant quotas and resource isolation for performance ([[capacity-provisioning]])
Agent tool contracts and action approval ([[tool-interfaces]])

areas.label: Safety & assurance
areas.question: How do we argue, enforce, and verify that a system will not cause unacceptable harm?
areas.scope: Identifying hazards, bounding the operating domain, enforcing safety at runtime, verifying and validating behavior, and arguing acceptable residual risk against recognized standards.

subjects.label: Hazard analysis & operating domains
subjects.definition: Identifying how a system can contribute to harm, including hazards from functional insufficiency rather than faults, and fixing the operating conditions within which safety claims are made.
includes: Hazard identification and analysis (STPA, FMEA, fault trees) applied to learned components.
Operational design domains and triggering conditions for functional insufficiency (SOTIF).

subjects.label: Runtime assurance & safety filters
subjects.definition: Mechanisms that monitor a learned component at run time and override, constrain, or replace its outputs so the system stays within a verified safe set.
includes: Safety filters, control barrier functions, Simplex switching, and fallback to a minimal-risk condition.
Input and output guardrails that block or rewrite unsafe generated content or actions.
excludes: Retry, failover, and graceful degradation for availability ([[reliability]])

subjects.label: Safety verification & validation
subjects.definition: Producing evidence that a system meets its safety requirements across its operating domain, through scenario testing, falsification, formal proof, and statistical validation of rare failures.
includes: Scenario coverage, simulation-based falsification, and software/hardware-in-the-loop qualification.
Formal and statistical guarantees, including verification of neural networks and rare-event estimation.

subjects.label: Safety cases, standards & certification
subjects.definition: Structured arguments that a system is acceptably safe for a defined use, the standards that set what evidence is required, and the field indicators that keep the argument valid after release.
includes: Safety-case structure and notation (claims, arguments, evidence; GSN).
Functional-safety and autonomy standards (ISO 26262, IEC 61508, ISO 21448, UL 4600) and integrity levels.
excludes: Regulatory compliance not specific to safety, such as the EU AI Act ([[governance-regulation]])

areas.label: Responsible AI
areas.question: How do we ensure the system's outcomes are fair, accountable, transparent, and governed?
areas.scope: Measuring and mitigating unfair outcomes, explaining and documenting models and data, keeping people able to oversee and contest decisions, and governing AI risk under organizational and legal regimes.

subjects.label: Fairness & bias
subjects.definition: Specifying, measuring, and mitigating how a system's outcomes and errors differ across people and groups.
includes: Group and individual fairness criteria and the metrics that operationalize them.
Pre-, in-, and post-processing mitigation and its accuracy cost.

subjects.label: Explainability & documentation
subjects.definition: Making model behavior understandable to the people who build, deploy, and are affected by it, through explanations, interpretable models, and standardized documentation of models and data.
includes: Post-hoc explanations (feature attribution, counterfactuals) and inherently interpretable models.
Model cards, datasheets, and the serving cost of producing explanations.

subjects.label: Human oversight & contestability
subjects.definition: Arrangements that let people supervise, intervene in, take over from, and challenge consequential system decisions, and the human-factors limits on doing so.
includes: Human-in-the-loop and on-the-loop control, recourse and appeal, and control handover.
Automation bias, complacency, and the ironies of automation.
excludes: The mechanics of agent approval gates ([[agent-harness]])

subjects.label: AI governance, audit & regulation
subjects.definition: Organizational and legal mechanisms that identify, assess, and control AI risk across a system's life, including risk-management frameworks, impact assessments, audits, and regulation.
includes: NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001 management systems; internal and external audits.
Risk-tiered regulation (EU AI Act) and frontier-model capability thresholds.
excludes: Data-protection mechanisms such as differential privacy ([[security-privacy]])

areas.label: Sustainability & cost
areas.question: What does the system cost in energy, carbon, water, and money over its lifetime?
areas.scope: Accounting for environmental and monetary consequences of ML systems under declared boundaries, and the decisions that reduce them per useful outcome.

subjects.label: Energy & carbon accounting
subjects.definition: Measuring the energy a workload consumes and converting it to operational emissions under declared boundaries, and scheduling work to reduce both.
includes: Energy measurement and energy efficiency (work per joule)
Grid carbon intensity and operational carbon
Carbon-aware placement and scheduling
excludes: Manufacturing emissions and hardware end of life ([[embodied-lifecycle]])

subjects.label: Embodied carbon & lifecycle impact
subjects.definition: Environmental impacts beyond operating energy, from manufacturing emissions and water to hardware lifetime and disposal, assessed over the full hardware lifecycle.
includes: Embodied carbon and lifecycle assessment
Water consumption of training and serving
Hardware lifetime, refresh, and e-waste

subjects.label: Cost, TCO & unit economics
subjects.definition: Monetary accounting for ML systems, from total cost of ownership to cost per token or accepted outcome, and the architectural choices that lower cost at fixed quality.
includes: Total cost of ownership and cost attribution (FinOps)
Cost per token and cost per accepted outcome
Model routing and cascades chosen for cost

groups.label: System types
groups.question: What is distinctive when the system acts as an agent or in the physical world?

areas.label: Agentic systems
areas.question: What does it take to engineer models that plan and act through tools over many steps?
areas.scope: Context engineering and agent memory, tool and action interfaces, the agent harness and its control loop, durable agent state, and multi-agent coordination.

subjects.label: Context engineering & agent memory
subjects.definition: Deciding what information enters each model call over a long task, and maintaining persistent memory the agent can write, consolidate, and retrieve across calls and sessions.
includes: Working-set selection, ordering for prefix reuse, compaction, and long-context degradation.
Long-term memory write paths, consolidation, expiry, and invalidation.
excludes: Retrieval and vector indexes in general ([[retrieval-rag]])

subjects.label: Tool use & action interfaces
subjects.definition: The interfaces through which a model acts on the world, including structured tool calls, tool discovery protocols, computer use, and the effects and authority those actions carry.
includes: Tool schemas, preconditions, function calling, and MCP-style discovery.
Computer-use agents and the handling of irreversible effects.

subjects.label: Agent harness & control loop
subjects.definition: The runtime that owns an agent's loop of model calls and tool actions, enforcing budgets, stopping rules, and approval gates and recording the trajectory.
includes: Reason-act loops, workflows versus model-directed loops, and plan revision.
Turn, token, time, and spend budgets; stopping rules; human approval gates.
excludes: Inference-time search and reasoning budgets per call ([[test-time-compute]])

subjects.label: Durable execution & agent state
subjects.definition: Persisting an agent's progress so long-running trajectories survive crashes, pauses, and redeployments without repeating completed effects, and can be replayed for debugging.
includes: Event-sourced trajectory logs, resume protocols, and record-and-replay.
Pausing for human or external events and resuming safely.

subjects.label: Multi-agent orchestration
subjects.definition: Decomposing a task across several model-driven agents and coordinating their delegation, shared state, and results, including when coordination costs outweigh the benefit.
includes: Orchestrator-worker and peer topologies, typed task envelopes, and delegation.
Coordination failures and correlated errors among agents sharing a base model.

areas.label: Embodied & physical systems
areas.question: What changes when ML closes the loop with sensors, actuators, and the physical world?
areas.scope: Sensing and perception, state estimation and mapping, motion planning and control, real-time and mixed-criticality computing, and robot learning from demonstration and simulation.

subjects.label: Sensing, perception & fusion
subjects.definition: Turning time-stamped measurements from physical sensors into task-relevant estimates of the scene, including calibration, synchronization, and fusion across modalities.
includes: Camera, LiDAR, radar, event, and tactile sensing; calibration chains.
Detection, segmentation, learned depth, and multi-sensor fusion.

subjects.label: State estimation, localization & mapping
subjects.definition: Inferring a robot's and its environment's latent state and uncertainty over time, through recursive filtering, localization and mapping, and learned predictive world models.
includes: Kalman and particle filters, tracking and data association, SLAM, metric and semantic maps.
Learned world models used for prediction and planning.

subjects.label: Motion planning & control
subjects.definition: Generating feasible, collision-free motions and closing feedback loops that drive a physical system along them under dynamics, contact, and actuation limits.
includes: Sampling- and optimization-based motion planning, task and motion planning.
Feedback control, MPC, and contact-rich manipulation.
excludes: Runtime safety filters over a planner's output ([[runtime-enforcement]])

subjects.label: Real-time & mixed-criticality computing
subjects.definition: Guaranteeing that sensing, inference, and control complete within deadlines on shared embedded hardware, and isolating safety-critical functions from less trusted ones.
includes: Multi-rate scheduling, response-time analysis, WCET, and real-time buses.
Mixed-criticality partitioning and hypervisors on shared silicon.

subjects.label: Robot learning & sim-to-real
subjects.definition: Learning robot policies from teleoperated demonstrations, simulation, and pretrained vision-language backbones, and transferring them to physical hardware.
includes: Vision-language-action models, action chunking, and cross-embodiment pretraining.
Teleoperation data collection, domain randomization, and sim-to-real transfer.
excludes: Imitation and reinforcement learning as general paradigms ([[learning-paradigms]])

concepts.label: System requirements
concepts.definition: Measurable desired behavior and constraints for a specified workload.

concepts.label: Baseline
concepts.definition: A reference method or system used to justify the value of a proposed change.

concepts.label: Proxy objective
concepts.definition: A measurable target used in place of the outcome actually desired.

concepts.label: Service-level objective
concepts.definition: A target for a defined service measure over a specified population and window.

concepts.label: Workload characterization
concepts.definition: The input, request, model, and execution distributions that a system must support.

concepts.label: Execution placement
concepts.definition: The choice of where system components execute, such as device, edge, or datacenter.

concepts.label: Data quality
concepts.definition: Fitness of recorded examples for the intended task, including validity, coverage, and error.

concepts.label: Label quality
concepts.definition: The correctness, consistency, and coverage of recorded supervision relative to the intended task, which bound the training signal and the trustworthiness of evaluation.

concepts.label: Feature engineering
concepts.definition: Constructing model inputs whose semantics and availability match the task.

concepts.label: Missing data
concepts.definition: Absent observations whose pattern and treatment can change learned behavior.

concepts.label: Data leakage
concepts.definition: Information unavailable at the intended prediction boundary entering development or evaluation.

concepts.label: Point-in-time correctness
concepts.definition: Constructing examples using only information available at their stated prediction time.

concepts.label: Data lineage
concepts.definition: Recorded dependencies that identify the sources and transformations of a dataset or artifact.

concepts.label: Training-serving skew
concepts.definition: A mismatch between the data transformations or feature semantics used in training and serving.

concepts.label: Dataset deduplication
concepts.definition: Identifying and managing repeated or near-duplicate examples.

concepts.label: Data selection
concepts.definition: Allocating learning effort to examples according to value, coverage, and acquisition cost.

concepts.label: Tokenization
concepts.definition: Mapping text into vocabulary-dependent token identifiers, which sets sequence lengths and so influences context usage, embedding size, and processing cost.

concepts.label: Distribution shift
concepts.definition: A difference between development and deployment data-generating distributions.

concepts.label: Linear models
concepts.definition: Models whose score is linear in their supplied features, with a possible output link function.

concepts.label: Tree ensembles
concepts.definition: Collections of decision trees whose branch traversal and aggregation determine predictions.

concepts.label: Kernel methods
concepts.definition: Models using similarity functions whose storage and evaluation costs depend on their representation.

concepts.label: Nearest-neighbor models
concepts.definition: Predictions or retrieval based on similarity to stored examples or vectors.

concepts.label: Neural networks
concepts.definition: Parameterized compositions of differentiable operations used to learn representations and predictions.

concepts.label: Inductive bias
concepts.definition: Structural assumptions that favor some learned functions over others.

concepts.label: Embeddings
concepts.definition: Vector representations whose dimension and lookup or construction method affect storage and computation.

concepts.label: Attention
concepts.definition: Input-dependent aggregation of value vectors using query-key compatibility scores.

concepts.label: Position encoding
concepts.definition: Representations that make sequence position available to a model.

concepts.label: Training loss
concepts.definition: A computable criterion optimized on training examples.

concepts.label: Automatic differentiation
concepts.definition: Computing derivatives by composing local derivative rules through an execution graph.

concepts.label: Optimization algorithm
concepts.definition: A rule that uses training information to update model parameters and optimizer state.

concepts.label: Regularization
concepts.definition: Constraints or training procedures used to control sensitivity and generalization behavior.

concepts.label: Training batch size
concepts.definition: The number of examples contributing to an optimization update or microstep.

concepts.label: Training state
concepts.definition: The parameters, gradients, optimizer variables, and other state needed to continue training.

concepts.label: Activation recomputation
concepts.definition: Recreating forward intermediates during backward execution to reduce retained memory.

concepts.label: Empirical scaling laws
concepts.definition: Fitted relationships between resources, data, model size, and observed model performance.

concepts.label: Hyperparameter search
concepts.definition: Choosing model or training settings through a sequence of evaluations.

concepts.label: Experiment-budget allocation
concepts.definition: Dividing a finite evaluation budget across configurations, repetitions, and fidelities.

concepts.label: Transfer learning
concepts.definition: Adapting representations or parameters learned from one setting to another.

concepts.label: Parameter-efficient adaptation
concepts.definition: Adapting a model by changing a limited parameter subset or added parameterization.

concepts.label: Tensor layout
concepts.definition: The mapping from tensor indices to storage locations, including strides and materialization.

concepts.label: Matrix multiplication
concepts.definition: A dense linear-algebra operation whose tiling, shape, and precision affect execution cost.

concepts.label: Numerical precision
concepts.definition: The representable values and arithmetic behavior of a numerical format.

concepts.label: Numerical stability
concepts.definition: Sensitivity of a computed result to finite-precision operations and intermediate representations.

concepts.label: Mixed-precision training
concepts.definition: Training with multiple numerical formats and explicit handling of their range and accumulation behavior.

concepts.label: Quantization
concepts.definition: Representing values using a reduced discrete set with a specified encoding and approximation rule.

concepts.label: Sparsity
concepts.definition: A pattern of absent or zero values whose execution benefit depends on representation and support.

concepts.label: Knowledge distillation
concepts.definition: Training a student model using signals from a teacher model or ensemble.

concepts.label: Graph compilation
concepts.definition: Transforming a model or execution graph into an executable representation.

concepts.label: Kernel fusion
concepts.definition: Combining compatible operations to reduce intermediate materialization or dispatch.

concepts.label: Host dispatch overhead
concepts.definition: Host-side work required to launch or orchestrate device operations.

concepts.label: Memory capacity
concepts.definition: Available storage for concurrently resident state and intermediates.

concepts.label: Memory bandwidth
concepts.definition: The sustainable rate at which bytes move across a specified memory interface.

concepts.label: Compute throughput
concepts.definition: The sustainable rate of a specified arithmetic workload on an execution resource.

concepts.label: Arithmetic intensity
concepts.definition: Arithmetic work per byte transferred at a specified memory boundary.

concepts.label: Roofline bound
concepts.definition: A performance bound combining a compute ceiling with an intensity-dependent bandwidth ceiling.

concepts.label: Data locality
concepts.definition: Reuse of data near its consumers across time or execution locations.

concepts.label: Tiling
concepts.definition: Partitioning computation so working data can be reused within a chosen storage level.

concepts.label: Profiling
concepts.definition: Measuring execution to attribute time, work, stalls, and resource use.

concepts.label: Resource utilization
concepts.definition: The fraction of a resource's defined service capacity that is occupied over a stated interval.

concepts.label: Serial fraction
concepts.definition: The portion of execution that a proposed parallel or accelerated transformation leaves unchanged.

concepts.label: Collective communication
concepts.definition: Coordinated data exchange and reduction across a process group.

concepts.label: Data parallelism
concepts.definition: Executing model replicas on different examples while coordinating learning state.

concepts.label: Tensor parallelism
concepts.definition: Partitioning a layer's tensors and operations across devices so each computes a slice, reducing per-device state while adding communication along the partitioned dimensions, usually within a fast scale-up domain.

concepts.label: Pipeline parallelism
concepts.definition: Partitioning a computation into stages that process different microbatches concurrently.

concepts.label: Training-state sharding
concepts.definition: Partitioning parameters, gradients, or optimizer state across workers.

concepts.label: Communication overlap
concepts.definition: Scheduling communication concurrently with independent computation.

concepts.label: Network topology
concepts.definition: The connectivity and capacity structure that constrains communication paths.

concepts.label: Stragglers
concepts.definition: Workers or tasks whose delayed completion holds back coordinated work.

concepts.label: Recovery checkpoint
concepts.definition: A persisted state from which a specified computation can resume.

concepts.label: Consistent checkpoint cut
concepts.definition: A recoverable collection of distributed states with compatible dependencies.

concepts.label: Replicated-log consensus
concepts.definition: Agreement on an ordered state history under specified timing and failure assumptions.

concepts.label: Fencing
concepts.definition: Rejecting effects from an actor whose epoch or authority is stale.

concepts.label: Federated learning
concepts.definition: Coordinating model learning across separately controlled data holders.

concepts.label: Arrival rate
concepts.definition: The frequency and distribution of requests reaching a service boundary.

concepts.label: Service capacity
concepts.definition: The completion rate supported by a service under a stated workload and operating point.

concepts.label: Queueing delay
concepts.definition: Time a request waits for a resource before receiving service.

concepts.label: Tail latency
concepts.definition: A high quantile of a defined request-latency distribution.

concepts.label: Request batching
concepts.definition: Executing requests together to share work or improve resource use.

concepts.label: Admission control
concepts.definition: Accepting, delaying, or rejecting work according to capacity, policy, and service constraints.

concepts.label: Autoscaling
concepts.definition: Changing provisioned service resources in response to measured or predicted demand.

concepts.label: KV cache
concepts.definition: Retained attention keys and values reused during autoregressive execution.

concepts.label: Prefill and decode
concepts.definition: The prompt-processing and incremental token-generation phases of autoregressive inference.

concepts.label: Paged KV allocation
concepts.definition: Managing attention state in blocks to reduce allocation waste and support sharing.

concepts.label: Prefix caching
concepts.definition: Reusing compatible computed state for an identical request prefix.

concepts.label: Speculative decoding
concepts.definition: Using proposed tokens and a validating procedure to accelerate generation while preserving a specified output distribution.

concepts.label: SLO goodput
concepts.definition: The rate of useful completed work that satisfies the specified quality and service criteria.

concepts.label: Generalization
concepts.definition: Performance on relevant examples or conditions beyond those used to fit the system.

concepts.label: Evaluation split
concepts.definition: A partitioning protocol that separates learning, selection, and final assessment.

concepts.label: Model-selection optimism
concepts.definition: Overstated performance caused by choosing a winner using noisy evaluation results.

concepts.label: Evaluation metrics
concepts.definition: Specified measurements of predictive or task behavior, with explicit populations and aggregation.

concepts.label: Probability calibration
concepts.definition: Agreement between predicted probabilities and observed event frequencies under an evaluation distribution.

concepts.label: Statistical uncertainty
concepts.definition: Uncertainty in an estimated quantity due to finite and dependent observations.

concepts.label: Benchmark protocol
concepts.definition: A reproducible workload, measurement boundary, and comparison procedure.

concepts.label: Online experimentation
concepts.definition: A controlled intervention used to estimate effects on deployed-system outcomes.

concepts.label: Sliced evaluation
concepts.definition: Measuring behavior separately on relevant populations, conditions, or workload groups.

concepts.label: Selective prediction
concepts.definition: Predicting on admitted cases and abstaining or deferring the rest.

concepts.label: Artifact versioning
concepts.definition: Identifying the exact model, code, data, configuration, and dependencies in an execution or release.

concepts.label: Production monitoring
concepts.definition: Collecting and interpreting signals about deployed system behavior and health.

concepts.label: Staged rollout
concepts.definition: Increasing exposure to a candidate system through bounded release stages.

concepts.label: Rollback
concepts.definition: Returning to a previously accepted deployment configuration with compatible state.

concepts.label: Deployment feedback loop
concepts.definition: A deployed system's outputs changing the data or behavior encountered by future learning or evaluation.

concepts.label: Retraining
concepts.definition: Training a replacement version of a deployed model on updated or revised data, with timing and data chosen to balance staleness against training and validation cost.

concepts.label: Incident response
concepts.definition: Detecting, containing, diagnosing, and recovering from unexpected system behavior.

concepts.label: System observability
concepts.definition: Instrumentation that permits investigation of internal execution from recorded outputs, traces, and metrics.

concepts.label: Threat modeling
concepts.definition: Specifying adversaries, assets, interfaces, capabilities, and failure consequences.

concepts.label: Data poisoning
concepts.definition: Adversarial manipulation of learning data or signals to alter learned behavior.

concepts.label: Adversarial evasion
concepts.definition: Adversarially chosen inference inputs intended to cause harmful model behavior.

concepts.label: Privacy requirements
concepts.definition: Requirements governing the collection, use, retention, and disclosure of information about people or records.

concepts.label: Differential privacy
concepts.definition: A parameterized bound on changes in output distributions under a specified neighboring-dataset relation.

concepts.label: Fairness criteria
concepts.definition: Explicit requirements for how system outcomes or errors are distributed across affected groups.

concepts.label: Authorization
concepts.definition: Determining whether an actor may perform a specified action on a resource.

concepts.label: Execution isolation
concepts.definition: Restricting which resources and effects a computation can access.

concepts.label: Human oversight
concepts.definition: An arrangement in which people can understand, intervene in, and contest consequential system behavior.

concepts.label: Operating energy
concepts.definition: Energy consumed by a specified system boundary over a defined workload or interval.

concepts.label: Lifecycle carbon
concepts.definition: Emissions attributed to operation and embodied system resources under declared accounting boundaries.

concepts.label: Cost per useful outcome
concepts.definition: Total relevant expenditure divided by outcomes meeting a specified acceptance criterion.

concepts.label: Capacity planning
concepts.definition: Provisioning resources for a workload distribution and service objectives.

concepts.label: Agent trajectory
concepts.definition: A sequence of observations, model proposals, tool actions, and external outcomes for a task.

concepts.label: Agent planning
concepts.definition: Constructing and revising prospective actions in response to goals, dependencies, and observations.

concepts.label: Context window
concepts.definition: The maximum token span a model supports in a stated execution mode, bounding the history it can use and the longest sequences the system must process.

concepts.label: Retrieval
concepts.definition: Selecting relevant records from an external collection using an explicit query and ranking process.

concepts.label: Approximate nearest-neighbor search
concepts.definition: Trading exact neighbor recovery for reduced search cost using an index or approximation.

concepts.label: Hallucination
concepts.definition: Generated factual assertions or summaries not supported by the relevant source or evidence.

concepts.label: Tool contract
concepts.definition: A specification of tool inputs, outputs, authority, effects, and failure behavior.

concepts.label: Idempotency
concepts.definition: A specified operation's repeated execution having the same intended effect as one execution.

concepts.label: Compensating action
concepts.definition: An explicit action intended to remedy an earlier effect whose direct reversal is unavailable.

concepts.label: Prompt injection
concepts.definition: Untrusted content attempting to redirect model-driven behavior across an instruction or authority boundary.

concepts.label: Trajectory evaluation
concepts.definition: Assessing task outcomes, intermediate effects, and constraint compliance across a complete agent run.

concepts.label: Reward hacking
concepts.definition: Improving a measured reward through behavior that fails the intended task objective.

concepts.label: Physical dynamics
concepts.definition: The evolution of a physical system under inputs, disturbances, and constraints.

concepts.label: Sensor calibration
concepts.definition: Establishing how observations relate to physical quantities, coordinates, and time.

concepts.label: State estimation
concepts.definition: Inferring latent physical state and uncertainty from observations and a model.

concepts.label: State observability
concepts.definition: Whether distinct internal states can be distinguished through the available observations and model.

concepts.label: Observation age
concepts.definition: Elapsed time between a physical observation and its use in a decision.

concepts.label: Feedback delay
concepts.definition: Delay around a sensing, computation, communication, and actuation loop.

concepts.label: Worst-case execution time
concepts.definition: A justified execution-time upper bound under specified hardware and execution assumptions.

concepts.label: Feedback control
concepts.definition: Selecting inputs using measured or estimated deviation from desired behavior.

concepts.label: Trajectory feasibility
concepts.definition: Satisfaction of motion, state, input, and dynamic constraints along a proposed trajectory.

concepts.label: Contact and compliance
concepts.definition: Mechanical interaction whose forces depend on geometry, motion, stiffness, and damping.

concepts.label: Simulation-to-real transfer
concepts.definition: Deployment of a learned policy under differences between simulated and physical conditions.

concepts.label: Runtime assurance
concepts.definition: Monitoring and constraining execution using explicitly stated safety premises and fallback mechanisms.

concepts.label: Stopping envelope
concepts.definition: The state and clearance conditions within which a specified stopping response remains feasible.

concepts.label: Operational design domain
concepts.definition: The conditions under which a physical system's behavior and evidence are intended to apply.

concepts.label: Safety case
concepts.definition: A structured argument connecting claims, evidence, assumptions, and defeaters for a defined system.

concepts.label: Structured output constraint
concepts.definition: Restricting the syntax or schema of model outputs without establishing factual correctness or authority.

concepts.label: Data acquisition and sampling
concepts.definition: The observation and selection process that determines which examples and populations enter a dataset.

concepts.label: Data contract
concepts.definition: A specification of schema, semantics, validity rules, and availability for data exchanged between components.

concepts.label: Delayed outcomes
concepts.definition: Target outcomes that become observable only after a delay or for a selected subset of cases.

concepts.label: Decision policy
concepts.definition: The rule that converts model outputs and system state into actions, thresholds, abstentions, or escalation.

concepts.label: Robustness evaluation
concepts.definition: Testing behavior under explicitly chosen shifts, perturbations, faults, or operating stresses.

concepts.label: Supervised learning
concepts.definition: Learning a prediction rule from examples with target outputs.

concepts.label: Self-supervised learning
concepts.definition: Learning from targets constructed from the observed data itself.

concepts.label: Unsupervised learning
concepts.definition: Learning structure in data without externally supplied example-level targets.

concepts.label: Reinforcement learning
concepts.definition: Learning a policy from action-dependent observations and reward signals.

concepts.label: Imitation learning
concepts.definition: Learning a policy from demonstrated behavior and possibly corrective interaction.

concepts.label: Model artifact
concepts.definition: The learned parameters, structures, example stores, and metadata required to execute a model.

concepts.label: Failure model
concepts.definition: The declared classes of faults and timing assumptions under which a mechanism is analyzed.

concepts.label: Backpressure
concepts.definition: A mechanism that signals downstream saturation to limit or slow upstream production.

concepts.label: Privacy leakage
concepts.definition: Information about people or records revealed through data, artifacts, or model interaction.

concepts.label: Execution time
concepts.definition: Elapsed time for a specified execution boundary, workload, and operating condition.

concepts.label: Irreversible effects
concepts.definition: External consequences that cannot be fully undone by restoring software state, retrying, or performing a compensating action.

concepts.label: Dataset storage layout
concepts.definition: Organization of stored dataset records, columns, partitions, and metadata that determines which data an access reads or decodes.

concepts.label: Data ingestion
concepts.definition: Reading externally produced records into a processing or learning system under declared delivery, ordering, and timing assumptions.

concepts.label: Schema evolution
concepts.definition: Changing a data schema while explicitly managing how existing data and producers or consumers remain interpretable and compatible.

concepts.label: Test oracle
concepts.definition: A specification, procedure, reference, or informed judgment used to assess whether observed behavior satisfies stated expectations for a test.

concepts.label: Integration testing
concepts.definition: Testing interactions among assembled components against stated interface and behavior expectations.

concepts.label: Failure injection
concepts.definition: Deliberately introducing selected faults or disruptive conditions to observe system response under controlled experimental boundaries.

concepts.label: Dependency environment
concepts.definition: The software packages, versions, native libraries, and runtime configuration on which an execution depends.

concepts.label: Workflow orchestration
concepts.definition: Coordinating dependent computation steps, their data or control flow, execution conditions, and failure handling.

concepts.label: Experiment reproducibility
concepts.definition: The ability to repeat an experimental procedure and obtain results consistent with declared criteria when its inputs, environment, randomness, and execution conditions are specified.

concepts.label: Accelerator execution architecture
concepts.definition: Organization of arithmetic units, execution lanes or threads, scheduling resources, and local storage that determines how supported operations run. SIMD/SIMT, matrix units, and systolic arrays are distinct examples.

concepts.label: Memory hierarchy
concepts.definition: Arrangement of storage levels and transfer paths with differing capacity, latency, bandwidth, access control, and management mechanisms. The available levels depend on the platform.

concepts.label: Host-device interconnect
concepts.definition: Communication path through which a host and accelerator exchange data and control, with transport, topology, and memory-access semantics that affect transfers.

concepts.label: Power delivery and integrity
concepts.definition: Supply paths, conversion stages, limits, and transient behavior that must maintain required voltages while workloads and actuators draw or return power.

concepts.label: Thermal behavior and throttling
concepts.definition: Evolution of temperature under heat generation and removal, and the performance controls or operating restrictions that follow under a platform thermal policy.

concepts.label: Service-level indicator
concepts.definition: A quantitative measure of one aspect of delivered service, such as latency, availability, or accepted-output rate, computed over a stated population and window.

concepts.label: Error budget
concepts.definition: The amount of service-level-objective violation permitted over a window, used to pace changes and risk against a reliability target.

concepts.label: Latency budget
concepts.definition: An allocation of an end-to-end latency target across the stages of a request path, such as network, preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing.

concepts.label: Operation and byte accounting
concepts.definition: Estimating a workload's arithmetic operations and bytes moved per example, token, or step from model shapes, to predict cost before measurement.

concepts.label: Memory footprint
concepts.definition: The peak memory a workload occupies, summed over parameters, activations, optimizer or cache state, and runtime buffers.

concepts.label: Workload trace
concepts.definition: A recorded sequence of requests or jobs with arrival times, sizes, and durations, replayed to evaluate capacity, scheduling, or serving policies.

concepts.label: Cost-sensitive decision
concepts.definition: Choosing actions or thresholds to minimize expected cost when different error types carry unequal consequences.

concepts.label: Pareto frontier
concepts.definition: The set of configurations for which no objective, such as accuracy, latency, or cost, can improve without worsening another.

concepts.label: Transformer
concepts.definition: A neural architecture of stacked attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections and normalization, processing all sequence positions in parallel during training.

concepts.label: Deep recommendation model
concepts.definition: Models combining large sparse embedding tables for categorical features with dense layers, whose cost is often dominated by embedding lookups and memory capacity.

concepts.label: Diffusion model
concepts.definition: A generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process, producing samples through many iterative denoising network evaluations.

concepts.label: Convolution
concepts.definition: A locally connected operation applying shared filters across spatial or temporal positions, giving high weight reuse and arithmetic intensity.

concepts.label: Recurrent computation
concepts.definition: Computation that updates a hidden state step by step over a sequence, creating sequential dependencies that limit parallelism across time.

concepts.label: Normalization layers
concepts.definition: Layers that rescale activations using batch, layer, or root-mean-square statistics to stabilize and speed training of deep networks.

concepts.label: Mixture of experts
concepts.definition: An architecture in which a learned router activates a small subset of expert subnetworks per token, decoupling total parameter count from per-token compute.

concepts.label: Expert routing
concepts.definition: The gating function that assigns each token to one or more experts, such as top-k softmax gating or expert-choice routing.

concepts.label: Expert capacity
concepts.definition: The maximum number of tokens an expert processes per batch, set by a capacity factor; tokens beyond it are dropped or rerouted.

concepts.label: Load-balancing loss
concepts.definition: An auxiliary training objective that penalizes uneven token assignment across experts so routing stays balanced.

concepts.label: Active parameters
concepts.definition: The parameters actually used to process one token or example, as distinct from total stored parameters in conditionally computed models.

concepts.label: Early exit
concepts.definition: Terminating inference at an intermediate layer once a confidence criterion is met, so per-input compute varies with input difficulty.

concepts.label: Sparse and sliding-window attention
concepts.definition: Attention restricted to local windows or fixed sparse patterns so cost grows linearly rather than quadratically with sequence length.

concepts.label: Linear attention
concepts.definition: Attention reformulated with kernel feature maps so it is computed in linear time with a fixed-size recurrent state.

concepts.label: State-space sequence model
concepts.definition: Sequence models built on discretized linear state-space recurrences, trainable in parallel and run with constant-size state per step at inference.

concepts.label: Grouped-query attention
concepts.definition: Attention in which groups of query heads share key and value heads, shrinking the key-value cache and decode memory traffic.

concepts.label: Context-length extension
concepts.definition: Techniques that extend a trained model's usable sequence length, such as position-encoding interpolation followed by long-sequence fine-tuning.

concepts.label: Weight serialization format
concepts.definition: The on-disk encoding of a model's parameter tensors and metadata, governing load time, memory mapping, and safety of deserialization.

concepts.label: Model exchange format
concepts.definition: A framework-neutral representation of a model's operator graph and weights used to move models between training frameworks and inference runtimes.

concepts.label: Model export
concepts.definition: Converting a framework program into a self-contained deployable artifact by tracing or capturing its graph and fixing operators, shapes, and weights.

concepts.label: Model signature
concepts.definition: The declared names, types, and shapes of a model artifact's inputs and outputs, forming its interface contract with callers.

concepts.label: Ridge point
concepts.definition: The arithmetic intensity at which a roofline's bandwidth and compute ceilings meet, equal to peak compute throughput divided by peak memory bandwidth.

concepts.label: Compute-bound vs. memory-bound
concepts.definition: Classifying a kernel or phase by which roofline ceiling limits it, indicating whether more arithmetic throughput or more bandwidth would help.

concepts.label: Data-movement energy
concepts.definition: The energy cost of moving operands between storage levels, which grows with distance and typically exceeds the energy of the arithmetic performed on them.

concepts.label: Amdahl's law
concepts.definition: The bound that overall speedup from accelerating part of an execution is limited by the fraction left unaccelerated.

concepts.label: Strong scaling
concepts.definition: How time to solution changes as resources increase for a fixed total problem size.

concepts.label: Weak scaling
concepts.definition: How time to solution changes as resources and problem size grow proportionally, keeping work per resource fixed.

concepts.label: Parallel scaling efficiency
concepts.definition: Achieved speedup divided by the factor of added resources, measuring how much additional hardware turns into useful progress.

concepts.label: Little's law
concepts.definition: The relation that the mean number of items in a stable system equals mean arrival rate times mean time in the system.

concepts.label: Latency-throughput curve
concepts.definition: The relationship between offered load and latency, in which queueing delay grows sharply as utilization approaches capacity.

concepts.label: Arrival burstiness
concepts.definition: Variability of request inter-arrival times or sizes beyond a Poisson baseline, which raises queueing delay at a given mean utilization.

concepts.label: Compute-optimal allocation
concepts.definition: Choosing model size and training data quantity to minimize loss under a fixed training compute budget, using fitted scaling laws.

concepts.label: Training compute estimate
